`languageIsoCode` is the attribute that gives the language of a data module. It is written on the `language` element together with [`countryIsoCode`](/s1000d-stack/reference/s1000d/issue-7/country-iso-code/).

## Elements that carry it

In the 33 XML schemas of Issue 7, 1 element carries this attribute.

| Element | Schemas | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `language` | 28 | Required |

## Allowed values

The allowed values are decided by the XML schema. The default BREX (Business Rules Exchange) has no rule that lists the values of this attribute.

| Defined by | Content |
| --- | --- |
| XML schema | The type is `languageIsoCodeAttType` (based on `xs:string`). The pattern is `[a-z]{2,3}` |

## Meaning of the values

The value is an ISO 639 language code. A simplified language uses a separate code that does not clash with the ISO 639 codes.

| Example value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `en`, `ja` | ISO 639 codes (English, Japanese) |
| `sx` | A data module written in ASD-STE100 (Simplified Technical English) |

## Related rules

- At the end of a file name, the language and the country are written in upper case, like `_JA-JP`.
- A translated data module has the same data module code; only the language and the country differ.

## In this stack

| Operation | Tool |
| --- | --- |
| Read | [`list_data_modules`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/reader/list-data-modules/) and [`read_data_module`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/reader/read-data-module/). The value is in `language` |
| Write it when a data module is created | `draft.language` of [`build_data_module`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/writer/build-data-module/) |
| Create a translated issue | `language` of [`apply_segments`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/writer/apply-segments/). The data module code stays the same and only the language changes |
